mintAuthorization.question: Who is authorized to call mint()?
mintAuthorization.answer: Any address a for which _authorizedMinters[a].canMint == true AND _authorizedMinters[a].mintVersion == mintVersion (the current global version).
evidence: FlaxToken.sol:58 `function mint(address recipient, uint256 amount) external override` — NO onlyOwner.
FlaxToken.sol:62 `require(minterInfo.canMint, "phUSD: caller is not authorized to mint")`
FlaxToken.sol:65 `require(minterInfo.mintVersion == mintVersion, "phUSD: minter version is outdated")`
FlaxToken.sol:44 `function setMinter(address minter, bool canMint) external override onlyOwner` — stamps the CURRENT mintVersion at grant time (:45-48).
mintAuthorization.grantedBy: FlaxToken.owner() only — a third, independent principal from Antimatter.owner() and PhusdStableMinter.owner().
mintAuthorization.globalRevocation: revokeAllMintPrivileges() (:88-91) is onlyOwner and simply does `mintVersion++`. Every previously-granted minter instantly fails the :65 check. It emits only MintPrivilegesRevoked(newMintVersion) — no per-minter event, and neither Antimatter nor PhusdStableMinter exposes any view reflecting its own de-authorisation.

mustAntimatterBeAnAuthorizedPhUSDMinter.answer: YES — mandatory. And PhusdStableMinter must be one too. BOTH authorisations are required for a single annihilateFrom to complete.
reasoning: Antimatter mints the antimatter leg itself: Antimatter.sol:236 `_phUSD.mint(recipient, amount)`. Antimatter is msg.sender there, so Antimatter's own address must satisfy FlaxToken.sol:62 and :65.

The stable leg is minted by the minter: PhusdStableMinter.sol:232 `IMintableToken(phUSD).mint(msg.sender, phUSDAmount)` with msg.sender == the minter, so the MINTER's address must satisfy the same two checks.
confirmedByProjectTests: test/Annihilation.t.sol:40-41 authorises both in setUp: `phUSD.setMinter(address(minter), true); phUSD.setMinter(address(antimatter), true);`

test/Annihilation.t.sol:248-260 (test_revokedPhUSDMintRightsRollsEverythingBack) revokes ONLY antimatter's right and asserts the entire annihilation reverts with nothing half-settled — the stable leg having already succeeded does not survive.
mustAntimatterBeAnAuthorizedPhUSDMinter.failureMode: Clean revert with full rollback. The antimatter is not burned, the stablecoin is not taken. Liveness loss only; no value loss.

burn(address holder, uint256 amount).notes: Permissionless but allowance-gated (_spendAllowance at :79). Antimatter never calls it and never grants a phUSD allowance to anyone, so it is not reachable against Antimatter's transient phUSD balance.

otherSurface.ownership: OZ Ownable; transferOwnership/renounceOwnership overridden only to satisfy the IFlax interface (:137-146). renounceOwnership is available and would permanently freeze the minter set — including making it impossible to ever revoke Antimatter's mint right.

trustAssumptions: phUSD has 18 decimals — assumed by Antimatter and never checked.
phUSD has no transfer hooks — true at this pin; this is what removes the reentrancy surface from Antimatter.sol:236-237. If phUSD ever gains an _update override this assumption breaks.
Antimatter and PhusdStableMinter are both currently-versioned authorised minters; a single revokeAllMintPrivileges call by FlaxToken's owner disables both silently.
